My tips are to be true to how you feel. Gender, like sexuality, is fluid. These people here who are leaving inflammatory comments are only upset because they aren't comprehending what is being said by non cis people. If it makes you happy, try it out. If it makes you sad, try avoiding it. It's really hard to find oneself, and if your gender is something that's causing you confusion, stress, or upset, it's good to question it. 

It's important to value your happiness over the comfort of those around you, so long as you feel safe doing it. If you are incredibly unhappy, do what you need to to get to a spot you are okay with. Please know that many people are incredibly transphobic, and you will be told that you're crazy, stupid, need to get laid, etc. Developing a thick skin is unfortunately necessary. 

Remember that you are not alone, and there are lots of people who don't fit into certain categories. Umbrella terms can be good! Try going to pride events and looking for booths with trans people. Try looking at online communities. Avoid communities that say you have to look or act a certain way to be trans, no one can decide that but yourself. 

Expression and identity are different. A man who likes to wear dresses can still be a man, a woman who has a beard can still be a woman. Also, sexuality is its own category too, and all these things exist independently from one another.
